headline: Earnings jump as revenue holds flat; guidance raised

drivers.explanation: All three segments grew earnings y/y per the segment table — Sempra Texas Utilities, Sempra Infrastructure, and Sempra California all rose — more than offsetting flat consolidated revenue.

GAAP earnings benefited from $82M of unrealized derivative gains and a $20M held-for-sale tax benefit (SI Partners/Ecogas), versus a larger $97M Mexico FX/inflation drag and a $25M regulatory-disallowance charge a year earlier.
Adjusted EPS strips out the derivative, FX/inflation, and held-for-sale tax items above, so its smaller y/y gain reflects underlying segment earnings growth rather than one-off swings.

CEO Jeffrey Martin cited consistent execution across the management team. The quarter's strategic update: the 45% Sempra Infrastructure Partners stake sale to KKR remains on track to close in Q3 2026.

summary_short: Sempra's Q2 2026 GAAP earnings rose 70.4% y/y to $1.21 per diluted share ($796M) as revenue held roughly flat at $2,997M; the company raised its full-year GAAP EPS guidance to $5.02-$5.55 while affirming adjusted EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30.
summary_long: GAAP diluted EPS of $1.21 (+70.4% y/y) benefited from smaller one-off headwinds than a year ago — $82M of unrealized derivative gains and a $20M held-for-sale tax benefit versus a $97M Mexico FX/inflation drag and a $25M regulatory disallowance in Q2 2025. Adjusted diluted EPS, excluding those items, rose a more modest 30.3% to $1.16 on segment earnings growth. Revenue of $2,997M was little changed y/y. Capex ran $2,226M for the quarter. Sempra updated FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance to $5.02-$5.55, affirmed adjusted EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30 and FY2027 EPS guidance of $5.10-$5.70, and affirmed a 7%-9% long-term EPS growth target. The 45% Sempra Infrastructure Partners stake sale to KKR remains on track to close Q3 2026.
